## Compare strategic alternatives

Keeney and Raiffa's multi-attribute value approach models preferences over
multiple objectives before combining attributes. This package's foundational
functions accept one common `value` scale; users should construct and validate
any multi-attribute value function before entering values here. The data below
is a synthetic strategic-choice example, not a reproduction of a published
case.

```{r}
strategy <- import_risk_data(system.file(
  "extdata", "strategic-alternatives.csv", package = "risk.decision"
))
decision_tree_summary(strategy)
```

## Sensitivity to probability judgments

One simple sensitivity check changes the probability assigned to a weak
adoption outcome and reallocates the difference to expected adoption. This
shows how expected values move under an explicit change in belief; it is not a
full probabilistic sensitivity analysis.

```{r}
expand <- strategy[strategy$alternative == "Expand", ]
weak_index <- expand$outcome == "Weak adoption"
expected_index <- expand$outcome == "Expected adoption"

expected_value_at <- function(weak_probability) {
  adjusted <- expand
  shift <- adjusted$probability[weak_index] - weak_probability
  adjusted$probability[weak_index] <- weak_probability
  adjusted$probability[expected_index] <- adjusted$probability[expected_index] + shift
  calculate_risk_metrics(adjusted)$expected_value
}

data.frame(
  weak_adoption_probability = c(0.10, 0.20, 0.30),
  expected_value = vapply(c(0.10, 0.20, 0.30), expected_value_at, numeric(1))
)
```

## Show preference and uncertainty together

Expected value summarizes the modeled preference scale, while the point cloud
shows the probability and magnitude of each outcome. Neither should be
interpreted without the underlying objectives, assumptions, and stakeholder
tradeoffs.

```{r}
generate_risk_matrix(strategy)
```
